questions.q: In S3, is a key like "raw/orders/2024/01/15/part-0001.parquet" stored as a real nested directory path?
options: No — it's one flat string identifier; the console renders shared prefixes as if they were folders
Yes — S3 maintains a real directory tree under every bucket
Only if you explicitly enable a 'folder mode' setting on the bucket
Keys can't contain slashes at all
questions.explain: S3 has no real folder structure — keys are flat strings, and the appearance of folders is a console/tooling convenience over common prefixes.

questions.q: What's the difference between S3's durability and availability numbers?
options: Durability is the probability data is never lost; availability is the probability the service is reachable to serve a request right now
They're two names for the exact same guarantee
Durability only applies to Glacier, availability only applies to S3 Standard
Availability measures how fast an object can be deleted
questions.explain: S3 Standard quotes 11 nines of durability (data survival) and 99.99% availability (service reachability) — two distinct guarantees.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three reasons this lesson gives for S3 being the default data-pipeline landing zone?
options: Built-in SQL query engine directly on every bucket
Effectively unlimited capacity with no resizing step
Storage decoupled from compute, so multiple tools read the same objects
Low enough cost to store data before deciding what to do with it
questions.explain: S3 itself has no built-in SQL engine — that's what Athena and Redshift Spectrum are for, layered on top of S3.

questions.q: What is a 'bucket' in S3 terms?
options: A top-level, globally-unique-named container for objects
A single file stored in S3
A folder inside another bucket
A compute instance that processes S3 data
questions.explain: Buckets are the top-level containers; their names must be globally unique across all of AWS, not just your account.

questions.q: Which AWS services does this lesson name as commonly reading data directly out of S3?
options: Glue, Athena, and Redshift Spectrum
Only EC2
Only IAM
None — S3 data must always be copied elsewhere first
questions.explain: Glue crawls S3, Athena queries it directly, and Redshift Spectrum reads it without a copy step — this decoupling is central to why S3 anchors AWS data pipelines.
